result.topic_en: Faint pencil calculations on a minimal-surface problem: an elliptic-type integral with three branch points reduced to logarithms, power-law expressions in a parameter t for coordinate differentials, and a Riemann P-function expressing a solution K of a second-order differential equation.
result.transcription:
2 Gebiete[?], eine fortsetzung[?] und Umwandlung[?]
$u = \int \frac{\partial t}{\sqrt{(t-a)(t-b)}\,(t-c)}$
$a = \infty \quad b = 0 \quad c = 1$
$du = -\frac{1}{2}\log\frac{1-\sqrt{t}}{1+\sqrt{t}}$
$-\frac{1}{2}\log\frac{\sqrt{\frac{t-a}{c-a}} - \sqrt{\frac{t-b}{c-b}}}{\sqrt{\frac{t-a}{c-a}} + \sqrt{\frac{t-b}{c-b}}}$

$z\sqrt{\frac{\partial u}{\partial z}} = 1 \quad \sqrt{\frac{\partial u}{\partial \eta}}$

$-\gamma\gamma - \frac{1}{2}$
$K = P\begin{pmatrix} \frac{1}{4}-\frac{\alpha}{2} & \frac{1}{4}-\frac{\beta}{2} & -\frac{\gamma}{2} & \\ \frac{1}{4}+\frac{\alpha}{2} & \frac{1}{4}+\frac{\beta}{2} & +\frac{\gamma}{2} & t \end{pmatrix}$

methods.what: Integral with three singular points used as a mapping function
Evaluation of the integral by logarithms for normalized points a=∞, b=0, c=1
General logarithmic closed form for arbitrary a, b, c
Power-law behaviour of coordinate differentials near a singular point in terms of the parameter t
Second-order differential equation for K with singular-point exponent terms (1/4 - α²) etc.
Solution expressed as a Riemann P-function with given exponents
